fields.name: SOLAR_LONGITUDE_ANGLE
fields.description: Solar azimuth angle relative to M2020 local level frame rotated 180 degrees over the X axis (+X points to the local north direction; +Z points up; +Y completes the right handed frame, pointing to the local west direction; the origin is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover) It is the angle between the positive X-axis and the orthogonal projection of the Sun onto the XY plane. It increases in the counterclockwise sense about the positive Z-axis. Range of -180 to 180 degrees

fields.name: SOLAR_ZENITHAL_ANGLE
fields.description: Solar elevation angle relative to M2020 local level frame rotated 180 degrees over the X axis (+X points to the local north direction; +Z points up; +Y completes the right handed frame, pointing to the local west direction; the origin is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover) It is the angle between the direction of the Sun and the positive Z-axis. A value of 0 degrees represents Sun at frame zenith, while a value of 180 degrees represents Sun at frame nadir. Range of 0 to 180 degrees.

fields.name: ROVER_POSITION_X
fields.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the X-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

fields.name: ROVER_POSITION_Y
fields.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the y-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

fields.name: ROVER_POSITION_Z
fields.description: Rover position relative to landing site. It is the z-component of the rover position relative to landing site, expressed with respect to M2020_TOPO frame (+X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the outward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located at the landing site)

fields.name: ROVER_VELOCITY
fields.description: Rover velocity

fields.name: ROVER_PITCH
fields.description: Rover pitch, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +Y-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

fields.name: ROVER_YAW
fields.description: Rover yaw, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +Z-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

fields.name: ROVER_ROLL
fields.description: Rover roll, or counterclockwise rotation angle about the +X-axis of the M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame. M2020_LOCAL_LEVEL frame is defined as follows: +X is along the local north direction; +Z is along the downward normal at the landing site; +Y completes the right hand frame; the origin of this frame is located between the rover middle wheels and moves with the rover

fields.name: MASTHEAD_AZIMUTH
fields.description: Masthead azimuth angle. Range of -180 to 180 degrees. An azimuth angle of 1 degree represents rover looking backward, an azimuth angle of 91 degrees represents rover looking to the left, an azimuth angle of -179 degrees represents rover looking forward, and an azimuth angle of -89 degrees represents rover looking to the right

fields.name: MASTHEAD_ELEVATION
fields.description: Masthead elevation angle. Range of 0 to 360 degrees. An elevation angle of 1 degree represents rover looking down, an elevation angle of 91 degrees represents rover looking forward and an elevation angle of 181 degrees represents rover looking at the zenith

meda.method: Native sensor series remain separate. Plotted bins are unweighted means of accepted native samples in 300 LMST-clock-second intervals. No interpolation; empty bins are null. Sample means/ranges are not full-sol or time-weighted climate estimates. UTC bounds are from labels; LMST is from actual rows, not an invented UTC conversion.

location.description: Perseverance, Jezero Crater. Same-sol SPICE-derived ancillary coordinates relative to the landing site in M2020_TOPO: +X north, +Z outward normal; +Y completes the right-handed frame (west). Ranges describe the rover positions observed in this sol, not an areal weather footprint.
location.limit: Landing-site-relative metres, not longitude/latitude or DEM projected metres. No geodetic registration or per-sample position join is claimed; no map pin or weather surface is drawn.

caveats: ATS and pressure labels contain no per-row quality flags; finite-only screening is not scientific quality certification.
Pressure uncertainty label lists kelvin, which is inconsistent with pressure units; this field is excluded rather than silently corrected.
Wind, humidity and local dust opacity were not imported. No DER_WIND product appears in this sol listing.

dust.kind: HISTORICAL REGIONAL REPORT · NOT A FORECAST
dust.summary: MSSS reported lingering high-altitude dust after a regional storm subsided, with further local storms near polar caps and Syria–Sinai. No afternoon dust-storm activity was reported at the three active NASA surface sites during that week.
dust.limit: Global/regional historical narrative, not a geolocated Jezero opacity measurement, storm polygon or present forecast. This week is not contemporaneous with the MEDA sol shown.
dust.validation: Cached dated HTML report verified against title/week/release identifier. Source describes intrinsic 1–2 km nadir imagery, lower-resolution public movie, off-nadir blur and data gaps. No image pixels or numerical dust raster imported.

radiation.date_label: MSL RAD surface sol 1 · label start 2012-220T02:25:43 (7 August 2012 UTC)
radiation.summary: Verified PDS3 metadata identifies Curiosity RAD calibrated/decompressed ionizing-radiation observations at Gale Crater. Its detector B/E dose sections use microgray per hour.
radiation.reference: Numeric dose unavailable: the science-file transfer did not complete. No dose, astronaut effective dose or exposure budget is calculated. MEDA optical radiation is a different measurement.
radiation.limit: Gale radiation is not measured Jezero radiation. No Jezero dose map or exposure calculation is available.
radiation.validation: Detached label, archive README and errata acquired. Label stop time is UNK. No numeric science import; partial transfers remain excluded. Detector absorbed dose is not human effective dose.
